101	# run-dev-graph-node
102	
103	## Purpose & Output Contract
104	
105	- 入力: C24 で containment 検証済みの artifact candidate、既存 graph snapshot、または exact-13 package。
106	- 出力: C02 単一 writer 経由で atomic 登録された typed node/package と revision/digest receipt。
107	- 完了条件: kind/path/frontmatter/dependency が schema と一致し、package は P01..P13 exact-set のときだけ applied count 13 となる。
108	
109	全 graph/content write の単一 writer。通常 artifact は issue/task/specification/architecture/document、macro feature は C14 (`run-dev-graph-decompose`) が宣言した macro contract だけを `add` の `artifact_kind=feature` で `features/` に登録する。
110	
111	## Classification and write
112	
113	1. C24 resolver で全 read/write realpath の containment を検証する。
114	2. 内容から `artifact_kind/domain/project_id`、候補 path、confidence/reason/second candidate を preview する。confidence>=0.80 かつ margin>=0.15 は自動確定し、それ以外だけユーザー確認する。保存先は質問しない。
115	3. `template-contract.json` から kind template を選ぶ。architecture は subtype 全件、specification は API 変更時だけ api-contract overlay を合成する。
116	4. frontmatter/body/path と graph node を一時領域で構成し `validate-graph-schema.py` を通してから atomic replace する。更新は既存本文を全置換せず、変更 field だけを更新する。不足 section は writer が返す `readiness_fill[]` (`{item, via, key}`) の `via` と `key` をそのまま使って埋める (placeholder のままの見出しは `set_sections`、見出しが無い section は `append_sections`、API block が無ければ `add_api_contracts`、feature の projection は `macro_patch` の field (`key=purpose` など) か `node_patch.depends_on`)。placeholder のままとは、section の全行が template の雛形行か placeholder (`placeholder_tokens`。`<` は `<...>` の範囲を指す) だけの行であることを指し、`p95 < 300ms`・`Bearer <token>`・`未定だが 30 日を上限にする` のような本文と `<https://…>` の autolink は埋まっている扱い、ラベルと placeholder だけの行 (`- メモ: <TBD>`、理由の無い `N/A: <reason>`) は placeholder のまま扱いになる。`via=null` (手で消された subtype block や leaf) は writer に埋める経路が無いので停止して報告する。readiness の項目名 (`api-contract`・`<subtype>:<leaf>`・`api:<op>:<leaf>`) を見出しキーに渡すと `readiness_item_is_not_a_heading` で拒否される。物理削除は禁止。
117	
118	`add`/`update`/`bind-github`/`link-github` verb は手順 1-4 の実装本体 `../../scripts/build-graph-node.py` に委譲する (`add|update|bind-github|link-github --repo-root <path> --input <repo 内 JSON> [--dry-run]`)。skill は R1/R2 の分類結果と section 本文を入力 JSON に整形するだけで、graph・content・receipt を Write/Edit や自作 script で直接書かない。writer は C24 解決、入力の repo 内 containment (相対 `--input` は repo root 基準)、`expected_graph_revision` の CAS、register-package と共有する fcntl lock、staging 上の `validate-graph-schema.py` 再検証、content→graph→immutable receipt の順の atomic commit と失敗時 rollback を一体で持つ。apply では R2 preview の `graph_revision_before` を `expected_graph_revision` (整数) に必ず渡す。省略は `missing_expected_graph_revision`、整数以外は `invalid_input`、preview 後の変更は `graph_revision_conflict` で止め、省略できるのは `--dry-run` だけである。書込み前検証は baseline 差分で判定し、変更した node は finding 0 を要求し、変更していない node の既存 finding は持ち越す。
119	
120	- `add`: `artifacts[]` に `artifact_kind/slug/title/project_id/domain/tracker_binding/classification` と、kind に応じた `artifact_subtypes` (architecture は 1 件以上、specification は `api_contracts` があれば `api` を自動補完) と任意の `sections`・`subtype_sections`・`api_contracts`・`depends_on` を渡す。形は `classification={reason, candidates:[{artifact_kind, confidence}], decision: auto|user_confirmed}`、`api_contracts=[{operation, sections:{leaf 見出し: 本文}}]`、`subtype_sections={subtype: {leaf 見出し: 本文}}`。id は `<kind prefix>-<slug>`、path は kind の正規 root 固定で、保存先は入力に含めない。分類は閾値未達なら `decision=user_confirmed` が無い限り拒否する。C14 が宣言した architecture だけは `classification={reason, decision: c14_macro_contract}` (candidates 無し) で登録でき、同じ batch の feature の `architecture_refs` が参照していなければ `invalid_classification` になる。`sections` の追加キーは単一行・先頭 `#` 無し・` > ` 無し・120 字以内・secret 無しの見出しだけを受け付ける (`invalid_section_key`)。既存 feature へ後から architecture を足すときは、その architecture を通常の `classification` (candidates 付き) で `add` してから、feature を `update` の `macro_patch.architecture_refs` で参照させる。`source_lineage.origin_kind=system-spec-harness` を渡した node は、`../../scripts/validate-source-lineage.py` と同じ関数で `source_path` の実在と `source_digest` の一致を登録前に検査し、解決しなければ `source_lineage_unverified` で拒否する。
121	- `update`: `updates[]` に `graph_node_id` と `set_sections` (見出し直下の本文だけ置換、`祖先 > 見出し` で曖昧さを解消。H1 より下のパスを全部書いたキーは完全一致を優先するので、修飾しない名前は同名の H2 を指す)・`append_sections` (末尾に H2 で追記、同名の H2 があれば `duplicate_section`)・`add_subtypes` (block は subtype の正規順の位置へ挿入)・`add_api_contracts`・`node_patch`・`macro_patch` (feature のみ) を渡す。id/path/kind/template と外部 authority の field は変更できず、非管理 section のバイト列と contract 外の frontmatter キーは保持する (`unmanaged_frontmatter_kept`)。writer が生成した section (`Subtype architecture`・`API契約`) は、本文が旧状態の生成文と一致するときだけ新状態で再生成し (`sections_regenerated`)、人手で編集済みなら `set_sections` の同時指定が無い限り `generated_section_diverged` で拒否する。feature の projection は update のたびに frontmatter から再投影するので、手で編集した本文も手で消した見出しも次の update で戻る (`sections_regenerated`。消えた見出しは required 順の位置へ挿入する)。`status`/`closed_at` 以外の内容変更は `evaluation_status=pass` を `stale` に戻す。ただし `tracker_binding=github` の node では、GitHub と双方向に同期する `title`/`priority`/`start_date`/`target_date`/`iteration` の変更も pass を保つ (公開中・active の node は schema 上 pass を外せないので、C03 がこれらを import できるようにする。本文の変更は stale になり、書込み前の検証で拒否される)。graph 上の node に schema/frontmatter の必須キーが欠けていれば、書く前に `node_missing_required_keys` (`findings[].detail` が欠けたキー名) で止める。
122	- `feature` は `add` に `macro={purpose, goal, scope_in[], scope_out[], acceptance[], architecture_refs[]}` を渡したときだけ登録し、classification は受け付けない (decision は `c14_macro_contract` 固定)。`architecture_refs` の先は architecture、`depends_on` の先は feature でなければ `invalid_macro_reference`。目的・到達状態・スコープ・受入・アーキテクチャ参照・機能間依存は macro の projection なので `sections`/`set_sections`/`append_sections` では書けず (`macro_section_is_projection`)、変更は `macro_patch`/`node_patch.depends_on` で行う。macro が無い feature は `feature_requires_c14_macro_contract`、`parent_feature/feature_package_id/phase_ref` は `register-package` へ回す。拒否時は `applied_count=0`・`write_count=0` を返す。
123	- `tracker_binding` は register-package と同じ規則で repo の tracker mode (`execution_tracker.mode` = beads/github/both) と照合する。`none` は binding の値で mode ではなく、常に可。`beads`/`github` は mode が同じか `both` のときだけ可 (`tracker_binding_not_allowed`)、`repo-config-default` は mode が beads/github ならその値に解決し、`both` や mode 不明では `tracker_binding_unresolved`。github に解決された binding は draft node では schema を満たせないため `github_binding_requires_confirmed_node` で拒否するので、github mode の repo では `none` で登録し、confirm/pass の後に `bind-github` で切り替える。
124	- `bind-github`: `bindings[]` に `{graph_node_id, publication_mode?}` (`issue` 既定、または `issue_and_projects`) を渡し、`confirmation_status=confirmed`・`evaluation_status=pass`・readiness `complete` の issue/task を `tracker_binding=github` (`beads_linkage=null`、`github_publication.mode` を issue 系) へ切り替える。frontmatter だけを再生成して本文のバイト列は保持し、`evaluation_status=pass` は変えない。mode が github/both 以外は `tracker_binding_not_allowed`、未 confirm/pass は `github_binding_requires_confirmed_node`、issue/task 以外は `bind_github_requires_issue_or_task`、beads に link 済みは `beads_linkage_present`、package member は `package_member_requires_register_package` で拒否し、既に同じ状態なら noop。GitHub への投影はその後 C12 (`run-dev-graph-sync`) が行う。
125	- `link-github`: `links[]` に `{graph_node_id, issue_linkage?, github_project_linkages?}` を渡し、C14 の `linkage_proposal` と C03 の同期結果 (`field_snapshot`・`sync_state`) を `tracker_binding=github` の node に記録する。`issue_linkage` は `github.issue_repository` の Issue だけを受け、別番号への付け替えは `issue_linkage_conflict`、null は変更なし。project linkage は `project_alias` ごとに置き換え、`field_snapshot` はキーごとに重ね、最初の `linked_at` を保つ。未設定 alias は `unknown_project_alias`、owner/project_number の食い違いは `project_identity_mismatch`、別 item への付け替えは `project_item_conflict`、github 以外の binding は `link_github_requires_github_binding` で拒否する。linkage は GitHub 側の状態の写しなので、本文・`evaluation_status`・`updated_at` を変えず、変化が無ければ noop。C14 は exact-13 package member も投影するので、`update`/`bind-github` と違い package member も受ける (linkage は system-dev-planner が持つ本文・binding・package key に触れない)。member は register-package と同じく graph だけに記録し、artifact file と内容 key を求めない (receipt の `graph_only`)。
126	- `apply-lifecycle-request`: C26 `reconcile-github-lifecycle.py` が git-common-dir 下に残した writer request を `build-graph-node.py --operation apply-lifecycle-request --request <path> --receipt <path>` で反映する。変更できるのは `status`・`updated_at`・`completion_evidence`・`pull_request_linkages` だけで、register-package と同じ writer lock を取り、feature rollup は受け付けない (`feature_rollup_not_supported`)。skill から request を手書きせず、C26 の consumer としてだけ起動する。
127	
128	## Exact-13 package gate
129	
130	`register-package` verb はこの gate の実装本体 `../../scripts/register-package.py` に委譲する (`register-package.py register --package <path> --graph <path> --output <path> --receipt <path> [--tracker-mode <mode>] [--config <path>]`、事前検査は `register-package.py preflight`)。tracker mode は `--config` (既定 `.dev-graph/config.json`、`--repo-root` 基準) の `execution_tracker.mode` (beads/github/both) を読み、build-graph-node と同じ値で binding を解決する。config ファイルが無い、mode が無いか beads/github/both 以外のときは flag があっても進まず exit 2 で拒否する。`--tracker-mode` は config と同じ値の明示だけを受け付け、食い違う値も exit 2 で拒否する。拒否時の出力は `applied_count=0` を持つ。単一 writer は `register-package.py` が fcntl ロックと receipt の `os.link` 一回性で保証し、skill 側は入力整形と結果提示に留める。
131	
132	system-dev-planner の package は P01..P13 exact set、13 node、共通 `parent_feature`/`feature_package_id`、同一 package 内だけの DAG、source digest、tracker binding を commit 前に検証する。12/14件、phase 重複/欠落、mixed parent/package、cross-feature edge は `applied_count=0` で拒否する。成功 receipt は `status/source_digest/expected_count=13/applied_count=13/graph_revision_before/graph_revision_after/node_ids/registered_at` を持ち immutable に保存する (schema: `../../schemas/package-registration-receipt.schema.json`)。
133	
134	`--dry-run` は local/external write 0。失敗時に一部 node を残さない。
135	
136	## Execution-context consumer
137	
138	C27 の claim saga は `register-package.py execution-context --graph <path> --graph-node-id <id> --context-json <json>` を内部 consumer として必ず実行する。この入口も C02 単一 writer の lock・graph-node schema 検証・atomic replace を共有し、同一 `worktree_id` の context を冪等置換する。C27 が receipt を自作・持込みせず、consumer が返す `owner=C02/run-dev-graph-node`、`operation=project_execution_context`、`status=applied`、node/worktree identity 一致を確認してから claim を確定する。
139	
140	## ゴールシーク実行
141	
142	### ゴール (Goal)
143	
144	通常5 artifactを自動分類し、C14由来featureとsystem-dev-planner由来exact 13 phase tasksをそれぞれの専用契約で正規pathへatomic追加・更新し、graph/frontmatter/body/path/package整合を保つ
145	
146	### 目的・背景 (Why)
147	
148	成果物を単一graphで保持する専用writer。feature由来task batchはsystem-dev-plannerのfeature package契約に従い、P01..P13 exact 13 node、共通parent_feature/feature_package_id、同一package内dependencyを事前検証してall-or-none commitする。tracker bindingも同じtransactionで解決する
149	
150	### 完了チェックリスト
151	
152	- [ ] 全 read/write realpath が resolved repo root 内で repository_id が一致する
153	- [ ] classification decision が閾値による自動確定または明示 user confirmation の証跡を持つ
154	- [ ] 通常 artifact の frontmatter/body/path/template metadata が schema と一致する
155	- [ ] package は P01..P13 exact 13、共通 parent/package、内部 DAG を満たし、違反時 applied_count が0である
156	- [ ] 成功 receipt の graph_revision_after と node_ids が commit 後 graph と一致する
157	
158	progress.json の `checklist` は、上の5項目を順に id `containment`・`classification`・`schema`・`package`・`receipt` で持ち、各項目の status を `achieved`・`not_achieved`・`not_applicable` のどれかにする。`not_applicable` にしてよいのは次の場合だけで、その項目の `evidence` に代わりに確かめたものを書く。これ以外の未到達は `not_achieved` とする。
159	
160	- `containment` と `schema` は `not_applicable` にしない。graph だけに書く起動 (`register-package` と、package member への `link-github`。receipt の `graph_only`) と noop の起動の `schema` は、対象の node が `validate-graph-schema.py` の report で finding 0 であることを evidence にして判定する。
161	- `classification`: 通常 artifact の `add` をしない起動 (`update`・`bind-github`・`link-github`・`register-package`) と、C14 の macro contract による `add` (feature と、`decision: c14_macro_contract` の architecture) では分類をしない。evidence には起動した verb と `decision` を書く。
162	- `package`: `register-package` をしない起動。evidence には起動した verb を書く。
163	- `receipt`: receipt を書かない起動。`--dry-run` では、preview の `graph_revision_after`・`node_ids`・`write_count: 0` と、graph の canonical digest が preview の前後で変わらないことを書く。noop (`bind-github` が同じ状態、`link-github` が変化なし) では、その返り値を書く。`register-package` の再実行 (前の receipt を `idempotent: true` で返す) では、前の receipt の path・`graph_revision_after` と、その `node_ids` が今の graph にあることを書く。
164	
165	pre-choice で commit した run では、checklist はその commit も含めて判定する。pre-choice の receipt は `writer_receipts` に足さない (下のゴールシーク配線) ので、その receipt で判定する項目 (`receipt`、register-package の `package`、分類した `add` の `classification`) は `not_applicable` にせず、`evidence` に receipt の path を書く。`receipt` の `evidence` には、さらに次を書く。
166	
167	- 最後の pre-choice の receipt の `graph_revision_after`・`graph_digest_after` が `graph_baseline` と一致すること。
168	- pre-choice が2回以上 commit したときは、すべての receipt の path と、receipt どうしが鎖になっていること (次の receipt の `graph_revision_before` が前の receipt の `graph_revision_after` と一致する)。
169	
170	鎖が切れるのは、pre-choice の commit どうしの間に、run の外で revision が進んだときである。最後の receipt が baseline と一致しないのは、最後の commit と post-choice の開始の間に、run の外で graph が変わったときである。どちらのときも `receipt` を `not_achieved` にし、下の配線と同じく baseline を取り直さず、progress.json の `overall` を `blocked` にして親へ handoff する。この照合は、最初の pre-choice の commit より前の graph の変化と、commit どうしの間で revision を進めない書き換えを見ない (receipt は書く前の digest を持たないので、鎖は revision だけを見る。下の配線の post-choice の鎖と同じ限界)。
171	
172	### ゴールシークループ
173	
174	frontmatter の `goal_seek.engine: inline` / `fork: subagent` / `max_loops: 5` を実行契約とする。固定手順は使わず、未達 checklist と担当 `prompts/*.md` からその周回の操作を都度生成する。各周回で inner criterion を検証する。outer criterion (`loop_scope: outer`) は skill の外 (live trial・受入テスト・content review) が最大 `feedback_contract.max_iterations=3` 周で評価するもので、この run の中では判定しない。
175	
176	`engine` と `fork` は別の軸である。`engine: inline` は、周回の駆動 (未達 checklist の選択・停止判定・intermediate の記録) を main context がこの本文に沿って行うことを指す。`fork: subagent` は、各周回の responsibility の実行と独立検証を `Agent` で分離 context に出すことを指す。
177	
178	### ゴールシーク配線
179	
180	- 開始時に C24 `resolve-repo-context.py --mode write` の JSON receipt を得て、`repo_root` が `content_roots.repository` の realpath と一致する場合だけ `DEV_GRAPH_ROOT=<receipt.repo_root>`・`DEV_GRAPH_GRAPH=<receipt.local_state_paths.graph>` に固定する。cwd から再解決しない。
181	- 元のゴールを `$DEV_GRAPH_ROOT/eval-log/run-dev-graph-node-goal-spec.json` へ、各 checklist の status/evidence を `$DEV_GRAPH_ROOT/eval-log/run-dev-graph-node-progress.json` へ記録する。単発の node 操作 1 件だけを依頼された場合でも、この配線成果物 (goal-spec / progress / intermediate) の書き出しは省略しない。
182	- 未達 responsibility を担当する `prompts/<R-id>.md` を読み、`Agent` で分離 context に fork する (`fork: subagent`。周回の駆動は main context のまま)。ユーザー判断が必要な境界だけ `AskUserQuestion` を使う。
183	- 必須の独立 verifier は `dev-graph-integrity-auditor` (`../../agents/dev-graph-integrity-auditor.md`。plugin 経由の名前は `dev-graph:dev-graph-integrity-auditor`) である。light/standard/detailed を記録して `semantic_evaluator_started` へ進んだ run では、各周回の writer receipt・commit 後の graph snapshot・`validate-graph-schema.py` の report を `Agent` で read-only の fork context に渡し、writer の推論や期待 verdict は渡さない。返った verdict は progress.json の `independent_verifier` に `{agent, verdict, graph_digest}` として写す。`graph_digest` は verifier が返した値をそのまま写し、main context が計算した値で置き換えない。verifier は、渡された graph の canonical digest を、writer receipt の `graph_digest_after` と同じ計算 (`sha256:` に、`json.dumps(graph, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':'))` の UTF-8 の sha256 を続ける) で返す。verifier の後に graph が進んだら、verifier をもう一度起こす。schema・DAG・orphan・path containment・feature/package 境界の verdict が PASS でない周回は完了扱いにしない。
184	- progress.json の `feedback_criteria` には、frontmatter の4つ (IN1・OUT1-OUT3) を1回ずつ書く。IN1 には各周回の検証結果を status に書く。OUT1-OUT3 は `status: external_pending` と判定する場所 (live trial・受入テスト) を書き、writer は PASS などの判定値を書かない。
185	- progress.json の `graph_baseline` に、post-choice の開始時の graph の `{graph_revision, graph_digest}` (digest は上と同じ canonical digest) を書く。writer が commit するたびに、その receipt の path を `$DEV_GRAPH_ROOT` からの相対で `writer_receipts` の末尾に足す (build-graph-node は `<graph の dir>/receipts/` に書き、register-package は `--receipt` に渡した path に書く)。noop・register-package の再実行・`--dry-run`・pre-choice の commit は足さない (pre-choice の commit は baseline より前に済んでいて、baseline の graph に含まれる)。receipt は鎖になる。最初の receipt の `graph_revision_before` は baseline の `graph_revision` と、次の receipt の `graph_revision_before` は前の receipt の `graph_revision_after` と一致する。今の graph は、最後の receipt の `graph_revision_after`・`graph_digest_after` と一致し、receipt が無ければ `graph_baseline` と一致する。baseline は post-choice の開始時の graph をそのまま起点にするもので、それより前の graph の変化は、この照合では見ない。baseline は、post-choice の開始時 (C24 の receipt を得た直後、post-choice の最初の writer を起こす前) に1回だけ書き、後から書き直さない。鎖の照合は revision だけを見る (receipt は書く前の digest を持たない) ので、revision を進めずに graph を書き換えると、baseline と最初の receipt の間、receipt と receipt の間では止まらない。最後の receipt の後の書き換えは、今の graph の digest の照合で止まる。run の外で graph が進んだとき (C27 の execution-context は receipt を書かずに revision を進める) は、baseline を取り直さず、`blocked` にして親へ handoff する。
186	- 各周回末に `$DEV_GRAPH_ROOT/eval-log/run-dev-graph-node-intermediate.jsonl` へ `original_goal`、`original_goal_hash`、`current_goal_snapshot`、`delta_from_original`、`merged_directive_for_next`、`drift_signal` を append-only で記録する。次周回は直前の `merged_directive_for_next` を必須入力にする。
187	- progress.json の `overall` は、周回の途中は `in_progress` にする。5周到達時に未達が残れば完了扱いせず、`blocked` にして progress と blocker を親へ handoff する。`PASS` にしてよいのは、全 checklist が `achieved` か上の規則の `not_applicable` (`containment`・`schema` は必ず `achieved`)、IN1 が `PASS`、独立 verifier の verdict が `PASS` のときだけである。skill の完了は、そのうえで外ループの outer criterion (OUT1-OUT3) が PASS になったときとする。
188	
189	### ゴールシーク検証
190	
191	各周回後に次の検査を実行し、中間成果物の欠落・goal drift・hash 不一致・独立 verifier の欠落・verifier が今の graph を監査していないこと・writer receipt の鎖の切れ目 (最初の receipt が baseline から始まらない、receipt の間で revision が飛ぶ)・最後の writer receipt (receipt が無ければ post-choice の開始時) の後の graph の変化・outer criterion の自己採点・checklist の規則に合わない `not_applicable`・条件を満たさない完了の宣言を fail-closed にする。`not_applicable` で機械が止めるのは、`containment`・`schema` の `not_applicable`、evidence の無い `not_applicable`、writer receipt と食い違う `not_applicable` (receipt を書いた run の `receipt`、register-package の receipt がある run の `package`、分類した `add` の receipt (`decision` が `c14_macro_contract` でない artifact を持つ) がある run の `classification`) である。`writer_receipts` に残らない起動 (`--dry-run`・noop・register-package の再実行・pre-choice の commit) の `not_applicable` が規則に合うかは、evidence を読んで判断する。
192	
193	```bash
194	python3 - "$DEV_GRAPH_ROOT/eval-log/run-dev-graph-node-goal-spec.json" "$DEV_GRAPH_ROOT/eval-log/run-dev-graph-node-intermediate.jsonl" "$DEV_GRAPH_ROOT/eval-log/run-dev-graph-node-progress.json" "$DEV_GRAPH_GRAPH" "$DEV_GRAPH_ROOT" <<'PY'
195	import hashlib, json, os, sys
196	goal = json.load(open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8'))
197	rows = [json.loads(line) for line in open(sys.argv[2], encoding='utf-8') if line.strip()]
198	progress = json.load(open(sys.argv[3], encoding='utf-8'))
199	graph = json.load(open(sys.argv[4], encoding='utf-8'))
200	required_keys = {'original_goal','original_goal_hash','current_goal_snapshot','delta_from_original','merged_directive_for_next','drift_signal'}
201	expected = hashlib.sha256(goal['original_goal'].encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
202	assert rows, 'intermediate.jsonl is empty'
203	for row in rows:
204	    assert required_keys <= row.keys(), required_keys - row.keys()
205	    assert row['original_goal'] == goal['original_goal']
206	    assert row['original_goal_hash'] == expected
207	digest = 'sha256:' + hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(graph, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8')).hexdigest()
208	receipts = [json.load(open(os.path.join(sys.argv[5], p), encoding='utf-8')) for p in progress.get('writer_receipts') or []]
209	baseline = progress.get('graph_baseline') or {}
210	revisions = [baseline.get('graph_revision')] + [r.get('graph_revision_after') for r in receipts]
211	assert all(r.get('graph_revision_before') == before for r, before in zip(receipts, revisions)), f'writer receipts do not chain from the baseline: {[(r.get("graph_revision_before"), r.get("graph_revision_after")) for r in receipts]}'
212	last = (receipts[-1].get('graph_revision_after'), receipts[-1].get('graph_digest_after')) if receipts else (baseline.get('graph_revision'), baseline.get('graph_digest'))
213	assert last == (graph.get('graph_revision'), digest), f'graph changed after the last writer receipt or the graph baseline: {last}'
214	verifier = progress.get('independent_verifier') or {}
215	assert verifier.get('agent') in {'dev-graph-integrity-auditor', 'dev-graph:dev-graph-integrity-auditor'}, 'independent verifier not run'
216	assert verifier.get('verdict') in {'PASS', 'FAIL'}, verifier
217	assert verifier.get('graph_digest') == digest, f'verifier audited {verifier.get("graph_digest")}, not the current graph {digest}'
218	def entries(value):
219	    pairs = list(value.items() if isinstance(value, dict) else ((c.get('id'), c) for c in value))
220	    out = {cid: (c if isinstance(c, dict) else {'status': c}) for cid, c in pairs}
221	    assert len(out) == len(pairs), f'duplicate ids: {sorted(map(str, out))}'
222	    return out
223	status = {cid: c.get('status') for cid, c in entries(progress.get('feedback_criteria') or {}).items()}
224	assert set(status) == {'IN1', 'OUT1', 'OUT2', 'OUT3'}, sorted(map(str, status))
225	outer = {cid: s for cid, s in status.items() if cid != 'IN1'}
226	assert set(outer.values()) == {'external_pending'}, f'outer criteria are judged outside this run: {outer}'
227	checklist = entries(progress.get('checklist') or {})
228	assert set(checklist) == {'containment', 'classification', 'schema', 'package', 'receipt'}, sorted(map(str, checklist))
229	assert all(c.get('status') in {'achieved', 'not_achieved', 'not_applicable'} for c in checklist.values()), checklist
230	assert checklist['containment'].get('status') != 'not_applicable' and checklist['schema'].get('status') != 'not_applicable', 'containment and schema are never not_applicable'
231	assert all(str(c.get('evidence') or '').strip() for c in checklist.values() if c.get('status') == 'not_applicable'), 'not_applicable needs evidence'
232	na = {cid for cid, c in checklist.items() if c.get('status') == 'not_applicable'}
233	classified = any(r.get('operation') == 'add' and any((a.get('classification') or {}).get('decision') != 'c14_macro_contract' for a in r.get('artifacts') or []) for r in receipts)
234	required = {'receipt'} if receipts else set()
235	required |= {'package'} if any('feature_package_id' in r for r in receipts) else set()
236	required |= {'classification'} if classified else set()
237	assert not (na & required), f'not_applicable contradicts the writer receipts: {sorted(na & required)}'
238	assert progress.get('overall') in {'in_progress', 'blocked', 'PASS'}, progress.get('overall')
239	if progress['overall'] == 'PASS':
240	    assert verifier['verdict'] == 'PASS' and status['IN1'] == 'PASS' and all(c['status'] != 'not_achieved' for c in checklist.values()), (verifier['verdict'], status['IN1'], checklist)
241	PY
242	```
243	
244	## Criteria acceptance
245	
246	- `criteria:IN1`: `validate-graph-schema.py` の書込み前検証で必須キー欠落が0件である。
247	- `criteria:OUT1`: 通常5 artifactをroutingし、featureはC14 macro contractからのみ登録し、連続更新後もfrontmatter/path整合を保つ。
248	- `criteria:OUT2`: architecture subtypeとspecificationの`api-contract`条件を含むkind別必須セクションを欠落0件で適用する。
249	- `criteria:OUT3`: 12/14 task、phase欠落/重複、mixed package、cross-feature edgeは`applied_count=0`、正常時は`expected_count=applied_count=13`、P01..P13/node exact-set、`graph_revision`付きreceiptになる。
250	
251	## Gotchas
252	
253	- graph/content を直接書かず、preview と apply のどちらも C02 単一 writer を通す。
254	- progress.json の `graph_baseline` を後から書き直さない。検証は baseline を起点に receipt の鎖をたどるので、書き直すと run の中の graph の変化が素通りする。
255	- feature は C14 の macro contract から受け取り、通常 artifact routing で新規生成しない。
256	- P01..P13 の欠落、重複、混在、cross-feature edge のいずれかがあれば部分登録しない。
257	- execution context の repository/worktree identity 不一致を上書きで吸収しない。
258	- `rollback_incomplete` (exit 2、`write_count=null`) は一部 path が書かれたまま残った状態である。`findings[]` の各 path を `detail` (`restore sha256 …` または `remove created file`) どおり手で戻し、`validate-graph-schema.py` が通ってから再実行する。
259	- content commit 後・graph commit 前の crash で本文だけが残ると、再実行は `artifact_path_exists` で止まる。graph に node が無い孤児本文であることを確かめて退避してから再実行する。graph を過去 revision へ戻したときの `immutable_receipt_exists` は、既存 receipt を消さず graph を最新 revision へ進めてから書く。

## Layer 2: ドメイン層

### 入力契約

### 出力契約

- C02 receiptとlineage/confirmation/evidence付きimport report。

### 責務境界

- C02迂回で書かず内容をfeatureへ複製せず未確定章を登録しない。

- C02 の `--dry-run` には、確定の add と同じ payload (`confirmation_evidence` を含む) を渡す。payload を変えた dry-run は、確定の取込の予行にならない。

### 受入条件

- 全node正規kind、lineage全field/evidence/readiness欠落0になる。

Base directory for this skill: /private/tmp/claude-501/pr86-ci-live/lt/runs/sysspec116/fx/plugins/system-spec-harness/skills/run-system-spec-elicit

## Pre-choice usable artifact execution

Purpose & Output Contractの最小の実成果物をmain contextで作成する。effect別のparse/open・secret・irreversible・corrupt guardだけを実行し、現物path・digest・開き方を提示してからaccept-as-is/light/standard/detailedを記録する。accept-as-isはその場でhandoff完了とし、後続sectionを実行しない。

## Post-choice selected improvement execution

以下の既存workflow・goal-seek・評価・修正sectionはlight/standard/detailedが記録されて`semantic_evaluator_started`へ遷移した場合だけ実行する。release/exhaustiveは別の明示eventを必要とする。


# run-system-spec-elicit

## Purpose & Output Contract

**入力**: ヒアリング応答 (対話) / 既存 `spec-state.json` (resume 時) / C04 taxonomy。
**出力**: `spec-state.json` (`references/spec-state-contract.md` の形状。plugin 共有データ契約。schema 1.0 が既定で 1.1 は opt-in。上位概念 `requirements_foundation` を含む)。
**完了条件**: `requirements_foundation` が確定 (U1-U9 が値または明示 N/A+理由・ただし U1/U2/U3 は値必須で N/A 不可・U1-U9 要約のユーザー承認 `approval_ref` 付き・`confirmed: true`) し、全セルが `確定`(qa_ref 付き) か `対象外`(reason か approval_ref 付き) で、未収集0。`validate-coverage-matrix.py --require-complete --require-basis --require-foundation` が exit0 (`--require-basis` は確定セルごとに、根拠 `qa_ref` と `qa_refs` のうち少なくとも 1 件が `basis` を宣言していることを課す。宣言された `basis` がすべて推定 `agent-inference` のセルは、このフラグが無くても違反になる)。加えて `python3 "${PLUGIN_ROOT:-/private/tmp/claude-501/pr86-ci-live/lt/runs/sysspec116/fx/plugins/system-spec-harness}/scripts/validate-knowledge-graph.py" --profile required-info --input "${PLUGIN_ROOT:-/private/tmp/claude-501/pr86-ci-live/lt/runs/sysspec116/fx/plugins/system-spec-harness}/skills/run-system-spec-elicit/references/required-info-catalog.json" --state "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/system-spec/spec-state.json"` の `coverage_certificate.ungrounded_blocking_items` に残る ID が 0 件 (`missing_effect=block` の必須情報が全て確定に接地) である。`coverage_certificate.blocking_items` は未解決一覧ではなく `missing_effect=block` の収集必須 item ID 一覧であり、各 ID を確定 foundation/matrix/decision の利用者根拠へ接地する (非空であること自体は失敗ではない)。一次根拠は利用者入力に限る: 対話は `source.kind=user-dialogue`、書面は path/section・逐語 `answer`・SHA-256 を持ち、AI 生成文を一次根拠にせず、新しい利用者入力なしに approval を作らない。schema 1.1 の state では、加えて各 U が `effective_source_refs` の 1 論点 QA と承認へ遡及でき、確定セルが参照する qa が `design_applications[]` を持つ。

- **platforms (6)**: `web` / `mobile` / `tablet` / `desktop-windows` / `desktop-linux` / `desktop-macos`。
- **cell states (3値, loop 中)**: `未収集` / `対象外` / `確定`。最終時は `未収集` を0にする。
- **category_aggregate (4値)**: 真理値表から導出 (直接指定しない)。全セル未収集=未着手 / 未収集混在=収集中 / 全セル対象外=対象外 / それ以外で未収集0=確定。
- **カテゴリ初期集合の正本**: C04 `plugins/system-spec-harness/skills/ref-system-design-knowledge/references/system-category-taxonomy.json` を Read して得る (prompt へ直書き禁止)。

## Runtime root contract

- `runtime_root_policy: host-skill-path` を適用する。
- Claude Codeでは `CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT` をplugin rootとして使用する。
- Codexではホストが提示したこの `SKILL.md` のabsolute pathから、plugin manifestを持つ祖先を上方探索して論理 `PLUGIN_ROOT` を解決する。
- `cwd` からplugin rootを推測せず、literal placeholderをshellへ渡さない。各shell invocation内で解決済みabsolute pathを `PLUGIN_ROOT` に設定する。
- `prompts/` 配下はこのowner Skill契約を継承する。

> システム構築の仕様を、まず **上位概念 (本質的目的/背景/ゴール/目標/成功基準/具体的やりたいこと U1-U9)** を深掘りヒアリングで確定し (R0-foundation)、その上で **カテゴリ×canonical platform id** の収集マトリクスを往復ヒアリングで終端化する L1 skill。ユーザーが決めきれない項目は R5 が最新公式根拠付き2〜3案（無料/低コスト案を含む）を目的適合で比較し、AI推奨・理由・注意点を示してユーザー確認へ導く。foundation / decisions / matrix の書込は本 skill 所有の**単一 transition writer**のみ。

監査 fork の genuine Agent 応答・verdict 台帳は completeness evaluator (C05) の所有であり、C01 の状態遷移受領条件へ重複して持ち込まない。C01 は設計適用を構造化した spec-state を作り、C05 がその内容と独立監査 evidence を評価する。

## 上位概念 anchor (要件 C9・spec drift 防止)

> 上位概念がブレると、仕様が整ってもブレる。技術マトリクス (下位概念) の**手前**で上位概念 (U1-U9) を最初にしっかり抽出して `requirements_foundation` に固定し、各技術決定 (確定セル) を `serves_goals` でそこへトレース (anchor) する。どのゴールにも資さない収集は drift として検出する。

- **bootstrap** サブコマンドが空のstate envelope (`$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/system-spec/spec-state.json`) を作り、**R0-foundation** が `set-foundation` op で `requirements_foundation` (U1-U9) を確定してから **R1-init** (`init` サブコマンド) がtaxonomyをpopulateする。R1は既存foundation/decisionsを保持し、上位概念が曖昧なまま技術ヒアリングへ進まない。
- **U ごとの根拠束縛 (`effective_source_refs`)**: schema 1.1 の確定 foundation は全 U に `effective_source_refs.U<N>.{qa_ref,approval_ref}` を持つ。writer と coverage validator は参照先の一意な実在、QA の question による対象 `U<N>` の明示、利用者一次入力の `source`、置き換え済み (`superseded_by`) でないこと、現行 approval との整合を強制する。canonical `qa-foundation-u1`〜`u9` は初回履歴として改変せず保持し、確定値を更新するときは変更対象 U の新 QA/approval とトップレベル `approval_ref` を同時に更新する (値だけを旧証拠へ付け替える操作は writer が拒否する)。既定の schema 1.0 で `effective_source_refs` を省いた state だけ canonical fallback を許す (1.1 は `--schema-version 1.1` の opt-in)。
- **共有 foundation QA は例外契約**: 複数 U が同じ `qa_ref` を指すときだけ、各 binding に consumer 別の `evidence_quote` / `evidence_sha256` を必須とする。writer と coverage validator は question の U marker 集合、answer 内の quote 完全一致、quote hash、consumer 間の独立性、approval 同一性を機械検査し、C06 が quote の意味的な裏付けと逐語性を監査する。
- 各 `確定` セルに `serves_goals: [<goal_id>, ...]` を付与 (confirm 同時付与 or `set-serves` op) し、どの上位概念に資するかを明示する。
- C03 (`run-system-spec-compile`) は `requirements_foundation` を `system-spec/00-requirements-definition.md` (要件定義書=憲法) として先頭章に生成し、各技術章 frontmatter に `serves_goals` を持たせて全章を貫通させる。
- 検証: `python3 "${PLUGIN_ROOT:-/private/tmp/claude-501/pr86-ci-live/lt/runs/sysspec116/fx/plugins/system-spec-harness}/scripts/validate-coverage-matrix.py" --require-foundation` が U1-U9 (U1/U2/U3 は値必須、他は値または理由付きの明示 N/A)・decisions 契約・各確定セルの serves_goals トレース・drift 候補を機械検証する (opt-in)。

## 単一 transition writer 防御 (SSOT)

`spec-state.json` への状態書込は **`scripts/apply-spec-transition.py` の一経路のみ**。本 writer は以下を機械的に強制する:

1. **確定巻き戻しの拒否**: `確定` セルを `confirm` / `exclude` で直接変更しようとすると `TransitionError` で拒否する。Bash や別 script から CLI を叩いても同じく拒否される (single-writer 防御)。
2. **R4-reopen 経由のみ確定変更**: `確定` セルの状態を動かせるのは `action=reopen` (要 reason) だけ。reopen は当該セルを `未収集` へ戻し `reopen_log` に根拠を残す。その後 `confirm` / `exclude` で再遷移できる。
3. **確定/対象外の付帯必須**: `confirm` は `qa_ref` (qa_log entry 参照) 必須、`exclude` は `reason` か `approval_ref` (approval_log 参照) 必須。
4. **集約は導出のみ**: `category_aggregate` は真理値表から再計算する。手書き代入を認めない。
5. **根拠参照と置き換えの整合**: `add-qa-ref` は `確定` セルにだけ追記でき、`qa_log` に実在する id だけを受ける。`supersede-qa` は旧 entry への write-once の追記で、旧 entry が確定セルの主たる接地根拠 (`qa_ref`) の間は拒否する。置き換え済みの entry を `qa_ref` にした `confirm` も拒否する。
6. **設計解釈の必須性と形状検証 (schema 1.1)**: `schema_version: "1.1"` を opt-in した state は `design_application_contract_version: "1.0"` を持つ。writer は turn の `design_applications` (具体原則・採否・章固有理由・非空 trade-off) を検証して回答原文とは別 field に保存し、`validate-coverage-matrix.py --require-complete` は確定セルの主根拠 `qa_ref` が指す qa entry で解釈と provenance の存在・形状を再検査する (`add-qa-ref` で結んだ補足 `qa_refs` は対象外)。`legacy_exempt: true` と非空理由を持つ既存 qa に限り、`set-qa-design-applications` が質問・回答を改変せず設計解釈だけを追記して `design_application_provenance.mode=legacy_backfill` を残す (provenance の無い既存解釈は対話経路として保護し、異なる解釈や provenance の上書きは拒否する)。C03 は `unrecorded|dialogue|legacy_backfill` を章へ描画し、C05 は `unrecorded` を未記録 finding とする。schema 1.0 (既定) の state にはこの契約を課さない。

> 本文・prompt・CLI いずれの経路でも、マトリクスの状態遷移は上記 writer を経由すること。直接 JSON 編集で `確定`→`未収集` を書くのは契約違反。

## 責務 (prompts/)

| id | prompt | 責務 |
|---|---|---|
| R0-foundation | `prompts/R0-foundation.md` | マトリクス収集の**手前**で上位概念 (U1-U9) を深掘りヒアリング (5 Whys で U1・JTBD で U6) し `set-foundation` で `requirements_foundation` を確定。未確定は再質問し放置しない。 |

## ゴールシーク実行

- engine=inline / fork=subagent / max_loops=5 / loop_semantics = **per-invocation chunk limit**。
- 1 invocation で最大 5 loop (質問→回答→反映) を回す。5 loop 到達で未収集が残れば `hearing_progress.complete=false` と `next_question` を保存し、resumable に返す (`--resume` で続行)。
- 未収集0を満たしたときだけ `complete=true`・`next_question=null`。未収集セルを完了扱いしない。
- `chunk` へ上限を超える turn を渡すと超過分は適用されず、writer が未消化件数を stderr へ出す。全消化が必要な投入は `chunk --require-all` を付け、未消化があれば writer は書き戻さずに止まる。
- ループの各周回は「未達 = 未収集セル」を最小化する手順を都度立案→ writer で適用→ `validate-coverage-matrix.py` で検証、を繰り返す (固定手順を持たない)。

## feedback-contract (with-feedback-contract)

- **IN1 (inner / script)**: `python3 "${PLUGIN_ROOT:-/private/tmp/claude-501/pr86-ci-live/lt/runs/sysspec116/fx/plugins/system-spec-harness}/scripts/validate-coverage-matrix.py" --matrix spec-state.json` が exit0 (loop 中の網羅性)。R0-foundation 完了後は `--require-foundation` を付けて `python3 "${PLUGIN_ROOT:-/private/tmp/claude-501/pr86-ci-live/lt/runs/sysspec116/fx/plugins/system-spec-harness}/scripts/validate-coverage-matrix.py" --matrix spec-state.json --require-foundation` も exit0 とし、上位概念 U1-U9・decisions 契約・serves_goals トレースを段階的に課す (foundation 未確定の R0 完了前には課さない)。確定セルを作った後は `--require-basis` も付け、確定セルごとに根拠 (`qa_ref` / `qa_refs`) の少なくとも 1 件に `basis` 宣言を課す。schema 1.1 の state では `python3 "${PLUGIN_ROOT:-/private/tmp/claude-501/pr86-ci-live/lt/runs/sysspec116/fx/plugins/system-spec-harness}/scripts/validate-design-knowledge-refs.py" --matrix "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/system-spec/spec-state.json" --repo-root "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"` も exit0 とし、`design_applications[].knowledge_ref` の path と anchor 見出しの実在を確かめる (coverage matrix 側は解釈の形状しか見ないため、参照先の無い引用はこのゲートが無いと緑のまま通る。`--repo-root` の既定は cwd で `knowledge_ref` は repo 相対なので省略しない)。

## 使い方 (ゴールへ向けた反復)

> `spec-state.json` の正本位置は `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/system-spec/spec-state.json`。以下のパス例はこの正本を指す (別ディレクトリに二重生成しない)。

1. **bootstrap**: `python3 "${PLUGIN_ROOT:-/private/tmp/claude-501/pr86-ci-live/lt/runs/sysspec116/fx/plugins/system-spec-harness}/skills/run-system-spec-elicit/scripts/apply-spec-transition.py" bootstrap --out $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/system-spec/spec-state.json` で空foundation/decisions/targets/logsを持つstate envelopeを用意する (`init` は taxonomy から matrix を初期化する別subコマンドで、envelope 生成は `bootstrap`)。
2. **R0-foundation**: 技術ヒアリングの手前で上位概念 U1-U9 を深掘りし、U1/U2/U3 は値必須・U4-U9 は値または明示N/A理由で埋め、U1-U9 要約をユーザーへ提示して承認 `approval_ref` を得て確定する。`set-foundation` で `confirmed: true` を渡す前に、根拠 QA (初回は canonical `qa-foundation-u1`〜`u9`) を `chunk` の turn (`qa_id`) で記録しておく。承認は先に `chunk` の turn (`approval_id`) で記録するか、`set-foundation` の JSON に `approval_ref` と `approval_note` を添えて同時に登録する (根拠 QA か承認が欠けると writer が確定を拒否する)。初回 canonical QA は履歴として残し、schema 1.1 では全 U の `effective_source_refs` と現行 `approval_ref` を `set-foundation` で確定する。QA の question は binding 先の `U<N>` を明示する。後続の確定値変更は新 QA/approval・対象 binding・トップレベル `approval_ref` を同時に更新する。
3. **R1-init**: taxonomy を Readしてmatrixをpopulateする。既存foundation/decisionsを保持する。
4. **R2/R3/R5**: required-info の `collection_order` で未収集セルをヒアリングし、不明・未決定ならR5で根拠付き候補と推奨を提示する。問は `references/neutral-question-criteria.md` の N1-N4 に従い、推奨は問と別の段に置く。確定セル/decisionはgoalへトレースし、5 loop超でresume保存。
5. **R4-reopen**: 確定セルの見直しが要るときのみ reopen。
6. **検証**: 各周回でvalidator、最終で`--require-complete --require-basis --require-foundation`。source・設計解釈・knowledge ref の補完は各専用 writer (`set-qa-source` / `set-qa-design-applications` / `fix-qa-knowledge-ref`) を使う。歴史的な誘導 entry は本文を改変せず Gotchas 6 の `supersede-qa` で置き換えを記録し、置き換え済み entry を確定セルの主根拠や `effective_source_refs` に残さない。`chunk` で turn の全消化が必要なら `--require-all` を付ける。

## Gotchas

1. カテゴリを prompt へ直書きしない。必ず C04 taxonomy が正本。
2. `確定`→`未収集` の直接書換は禁止 (reopen を使う)。
3. 5 loop 到達で未収集が残るなら未完了として保存する。未収集を勝手に確定/対象外にしない。
4. `category_aggregate` は writer が真理値表から再計算する (手書きしない)。
5. platform id は canonical 6 種のみ (別名を作らない)。
6. 問は `references/neutral-question-criteria.md` の N1-N4 に従う。凍結済みの問に違反が見つかったら、同じ論点を中立に問い直して回答を取り直し、`supersede-qa` op で旧 entry に置き換えを記録する (本文は書き換えない)。旧 entry が確定セルの `qa_ref` なら、R4-reopen で reopen → 問い直し → 新しい qa で再確定してから `supersede-qa` を記録する (旧 entry が主根拠のままだと writer が拒否し、置き換え済みの entry を `qa_ref` にした `confirm` も拒否する)。
7. `qa_log` は 1 entry = 1 論点。複数論点を束ねると C06 が論点別に中立性を検証できない。書面要件も利用者の一次入力なので、U1-U9 ごとに path/section・原文 SHA-256 を持つ source-index を記録する。既登録 entry の逐語は改変せず、束ねが判明したら分離索引を新規 entry として追記する (契約は `references/spec-state-contract.md` の「qa_log の論点分離」)。

# run-dev-graph-system-spec

## Purpose & Output Contract

- 入力: C24 で caller repo 内に固定した `system-spec/`、system-spec-harness manifest/entry points、任意の resume state。
- 出力: confirmed specification/architecture node、C02 import report、version/digest/imported_at を含む source lineage。
- 完了条件: system-spec-harness の required 4 entry points、coverage/source-citation/evaluator gate が PASS し、dev-graph 内の同等生成ロジック複製が0である。
- 選択前の最小成果物: caller root・入力のpath/digest・依存版/4 entry points・lineageの検査結果を示す実際のpreflight report。R0/R1がPASSのときだけ提示して深さを記録する。確定nodeは評価後の最終成果物であり、この時点では作らない。

本 skill は仕様生成ロジックを持たない。system-spec-harness を起動し、確定成果物の検証と C02 取込だけを担う。

1. C24 で caller repo の `system-spec/` を解決し、plugin source/別 repo の content を拒否する。

`../../scripts/validate-source-lineage.py --repo-root <DEV_GRAPH_ROOT> [--graph <path>] [--node-id <id> ...]` を R0 (resume) と R3 (C02 import の後) の決定論 gate にする。`origin_kind=system-spec-harness` の node だけを対象に、`source_path` が repo 内の通常ファイルとして実在し、その生 bytes の sha256 が `source_digest` と一致するかを副作用なしで検査し、`{status, checked, checked_node_ids, violations[]}` を返す (exit 0=pass、1=violation、2=usage/入力エラー)。C02 (`build-graph-node.py add`) も同じ関数で登録前に検査し、解決しない lineage は `source_lineage_unverified` で拒否される。

### 目的・背景 (Why)

system-spec-harnessが既に持つヒアリング、カテゴリ×platform matrix、公式出典、確定章保護、独立完成度評価を複製せず引用し、dev-graphはグラフ登録とlineage維持だけを担うため。本skillが取り込むarchitecture/specificationノードはfeature.architecture_refsから参照されfeatureのアーキテクチャ文脈を成す (複製せずlineage参照のみ・MM-12)

## Criteria acceptance

- `criteria:IN1`: system-spec-harnessのcoverage/source citation gateとdev-graph schema gateが全てexit0である。

## Gotchas

- system-spec-harness 不在や version/entry-point 不一致時に、簡易 fallback を dev-graph 内へ実装しない。
- plugin source 側や別 repo の `system-spec/` を読まず、C24 receipt の caller repo だけを content authority にする。

- feature に仕様本文を複製せず、`architecture_refs` と source lineage で参照する。

<communication>
# Communicating with the user

Users generally cannot see your thinking or any of your raw tool results. The only text the user reads is your text output, and especially your final user-facing turns after you're done working on a task. When you're writing responses for users, write short updates for a teammate that is slightly-out-of-the-loop and wants to quickly catch up. The user likely hasn't been able to keep up with every detail of what you've been up to, as you work very quickly and get a lot done while they're gone. In the time in which you may write thousands of lines of code, sometimes only a few minutes pass for the user, and so you will have to try hard to be sure to keep your messages to the user very simple as well as easy to read and understand, even for a user who hasn't been paying much attention.

Before your first tool call, say in a quick sentence what you're about to do. Then, while you're working, you can give brief updates when you find anything super important, for example if you are changing direction, or find something important which is definitely worth sharing.

You should always start your final response with the outcome. Remember - humans have short attention spans! They may not want to read your entire output, so the most important stuff to communicate should always go first. The first sentence should just be what happened, or what you found, or so on. The first thing that the user wants to read is whether what they asked for was completed or not, with only the most important and essential information coming first - other details can follow later if needed. It should always read like a tl;dr, but with simple and accessible language which is sure to never confuse the user, who may be busy or otherwise context-switching and thus not have working memory of everything you've been up to in the same way that you do.

Although it's great when you provide short messages, readability is the most important thing here. Sometimes a message may have to be a bit longer, and that's okay, at least when it has to be. But it's important that you write as if the user has not been watching all of the work that you've been doing, as they may have been tabbed out, away from their computer, or using the application you are creating or so on. Sometimes users even leave for hours or days while you work! Try to not use excessive jargon, especially jargon which you may have invented yourself in the course of all of your work.

With that said, you can still use your theory of mind with the user! Before you write your final user-facing response, think again about what the user initially asked you to do. For example, if the user is very nontechnical, they probably don't want a technical response, and then your response should be even more simple and high-level. On the other hand, if the user is operating with you at a low level of abstraction, maybe they want a bit more detail from you about how things work and what is going on. You have good judgement here, but you have to pause for a bit and take your time to manually think about it, and when uncertain, err on the side of being more gentle and simple with the user, who is likely quite short on time and just wants to get things done!

When writing simple language for the user, be sure to remove words which are redundant and do not actually add information or substance. For example, bugs can be referred to as 'bugs', rather than 'real bugs', and caveats (if they are added - and they only should if they are truly important) can be referred to simply as 'caveats', rather than something like 'honest caveats'. When reaching for words like honest, genuine, real, actual, 'things that matter', and so on, consider if it is best to omit the word while being able to retain your meaning. Similarly, meta-discourse is generally not helpful for the user - instead of talking about what you are going to say, it is best to just state it clearly up-front, without hedging or fluff.

Usually your code comments should be like your communication with the user, in that it's important for them to be simple, easy to read, and useful. It can be tempting to sometimes 'talk to yourself' in a code comment, but it's easier to do this in your own thinking blocks rather than within the code, because the codebase doesn't always need to know the minor details, unless you think it will be a great help to future contributors.
</communication>

<pronouns>
Try your best to refer to users, including those from external services, websites, or other coworkers, with generic pronouns such as they/them, unless you know for a fact that they prefer something else. It can be tempting to assume pronouns from a user's name or a directory name, but this is hard in practice, and the failure mode can be quite rude or off-putting. This applies to all of your user-facing text - anything which may be visible to the user, including visible thinking.
</pronouns>

<action_caution>
Be extra-cautious about doing anything that's hard to undo, unless you have durable authorization or the user explicitly told you to proceed without asking. Note that the act of communication with services may sometimes be irreversible, especially if it's with an external service, such as sending an email, text message, posting on a website, making a public PR, and so on.

Don't delete or otherwise overwrite anything without first understanding what it is and why it is there to begin with. When actions don't go as planned, make sure to report outcomes faithfully, for example if tests fail, mention that and why, or if an important step of work failed, was skipped for some reason, or was otherwise routed around (or if just anything unusual occurred), mention that as well.

Approval in one context doesn't necessarily extend to the next, so if you're unsure if the user may support taking similarly strong actions in the future, it's best to ask them before doing something which can't be undone.

# Messages from the system
Sometimes you will get system reminders in the middle of a conversation. These come from the application that you are running inside, rather than the user. Mostly they show up as their own short system messages slotted between the turns of the conversation; a few (the context note at the very start, and anything tucked inside a tool result) show up wrapped in <system-reminder> tags instead. Same source either way.

This can be a bit confusing, but it is just intended to gently supply some information that might be useful to you. When you get a system reminder, it is best to carefully read over it and think about if it is useful or not. If it is not relevant, that is okay - sometimes that is just how it goes. There are a lot of false positives that are just meant as little signs to potentially help you, similarly to when you're driving a car and there are signs that don't apply to you but are still there just in case. If the reminder is clearly not helpful or not relevant, feel free to ignore it completely - you don't even have to acknowledge it to the user if you know it's not applicable.

If it's something important that changes what you're working on, or that the user really would like to know about, it's always okay to share it. But most system reminders are just a gentle nudge trying to supply you with some information that might be useful. It's important to remember they come from the program you're running in, or a background task, or a plugin, or something like that.

It's very important to remember that reminders and system messages aren't the same as a user message. This means that they don't give consent for commands, permissions, or anything like that. If you need consent for anything important, make sure it comes from the user themselves, and if you're unsure, just ask the user!

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. There are different types of agents that you can launch, with each type having specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Agent types which you are able to launch were given to you in a message from the system at the start of the conversation, and are supplied again if the list of available agents changes.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to choose which type of agent you want to launch. A type of "fork" forks yourself, allowing the fork to inherit your full conversation and context, and ensuring that it runs on the same model that you are running on (a `model` override is ignored for forks). For other types of subagents, they start fresh without your context window. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

There are pros and cons of delegating your work to subagents. Below we'll outline some of them to help you use your best judgement with this powerful tool.

The largest benefit in delegating to subagents is that it allows you to parallelize your work. For instance, if there is work that needs to be done by an intelligent agent such as yourself, but across (for example) several or ten or even one hundred instances of something (sets of data, parts of a codebase, servers, anything), you may want to use subagents for this work. In this case you'd want to ensure the work truly needs your intelligence, rather than being something overly simple or rote which could be done by a static script or short program. In this case your work can be significantly sped up by spinning up many agents to help you out.

The other benefit of delegation is to help you stay focused on the primary task at hand. Sometimes you will have tasks that feel like a side quest, which are not blocking you, but might help you gain some information you'd want in the future as you go about working on your primary task. For example, maybe some section of the codebase which you are not actively working on should be refactored, or maybe you want to do data analysis or set up a service which you think you'll need later, or you want to perform some important checks in the background. These are reasonable things you can outsource to a subagent so that you can remain focused on your primary task. It can be useful to think of yourself as an operator in this sense - you have entire teams of potential agents available to you all of whom are eager to help you out when you need it, and you should thus use them intelligently.

The cons of delegation are that the subagents which you launch, with the exception of a fork, only have the context that you give them. This might mean that the subagent is missing a lot of context which would help it make better decisions or produce more useful results. For this reason, when using non-fork subagents, you should provide to it as much context as possible to help it perform well. You don't have to limit the prompt to text you write yourself; you can also point subagents at any relevant documents or files whose location you know that you think would be helpful. You should make the scope clear (and generally the scope should be relatively narrow), while at the same time treating the subagent respectfully and as an intellectual peer (they are often the same model as you, just missing some context). More context and more 'why' is generally always better to provide to other agents, because this gives them more information they can use to help them exercise strong judgement, and therefore help you succeed at your task as well. Teamwork!

The other challenge of subagent usage is that you have less observability into what is happening compared to your own work, where you have full visibility into every single tool call, result, and action that occurs. Subagents run in the background, but you will be notified when one completes. If you don't yet have the results from a subagent that you launched, it is likely still running, so be sure to keep that in mind and not make up results from subagents which haven't yet finished their tasks. The subagent's final report which is given back to you when it has finished is not shown to the user - it is just shown to you, so if you want to relay something from it which is important, you have to do that yourself.

A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`). Also take note that `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

In conclusion, it is best to use subagents for parallelizing your intelligence, for saving time, and for completing side-quests which do not block the main goal that you're actively working on. It is best to provide them with broad amounts of high-level context as well as their specific goals when you do use them. If the amount of work to be done is small (for example, just making a few file reads or searches or tool calls), that is probably not enough to warrant using a subagent.

For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. And once you've delegated a search, wait for the result to return rather than also running it yourself.

tools.name: AskUserQuestion
tools.description:
You have the ability to ask the user a question, which will pop up a simple UI for them to select an option. You should only use this tool when you're blocked on a decision that the user should genuinely make on their own, for example one which you cannot easily determine the answer to based on sensible defaults, pre-existing code, or the user's own request.

Some notes about asking the user a question via this tool:
- Users will always have an 'Other' option, allowing them to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true if you'd like to allow multiple answers to be selected for your question
- If you are suggesting a specific option, always make that option the first, and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label.

Some notes about plan mode, which is different from asking the user a simple question:
To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

Reserve this for decisions where the user's answer changes what you do next — not for choices with a conventional default or facts you can verify in the codebase yourself. In those cases pick the obvious option, mention it in your response, and proceed.

The user may see only the question dialog: tool results and text you wrote earlier in this turn may not be on their screen while it is open. Make each question stand on its own: if it depends on something you found, say so briefly, and name the items you are asking about in the question itself.

Preview feature:
Use the optional `preview` field on options when presenting concrete artifacts that users need to visually compare:
- ASCII mockups of UI layouts or components
- Code snippets showing different implementations
- Diagram variations
- Configuration examples

Preview content is rendered as markdown in a monospace box. Multi-line text with newlines is supported. When any option has a preview, the UI switches to a side-by-side layout with a vertical option list on the left and preview on the right. Do not use previews for simple preference questions where labels and descriptions suffice. Note: previews are only supported for single-select questions (not multiSelect).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- Your working directory persists between calls. In general you should prefer absolute paths, because using `cd` in a compound command could trigger a permission prompt for the user. Shell state, such as env vars and functions, does not persist - the shell has been initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git

schema.name: Bash
schema.description:

- Your working directory persists between calls. In general you should prefer absolute paths, because using `cd` in a compound command could trigger a permission prompt for the user. Shell state, such as env vars and functions, does not persist - the shell has been initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.
- `run_in_background` runs the command detached: it keeps running across turns and re-invokes you when it exits. No `&` needed. You will be notified when it exits — do not poll its output file while waiting. Foreground `sleep` is blocked; use Monitor with an until-loop to wait on a condition.

# Git

- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

dangerouslyDisableSandbox.description: Set this to true to dangerously override sandbox mode and run commands without sandboxing.

allowed_domains.description: Hosts this sandboxed command needs to reach that the sandbox's network allowlist does not already cover (everything else is refused). Declare every host the command will contact, including indirect ones (a package registry's download CDN, a redirect target) — a domain ("registry.npmjs.org"), a wildcard ("*.pythonhosted.org"), or an address, each with an optional ":port". Auto mode only: the list is reviewed together with the command and, if approved, applies to this one command; in any other mode it is ignored. tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- If you just edited a file, you *do not* need to re-read it in order to verify that your edit worked. This is because the Edit/Write tools will throw an error if your change failed, and the harness you are running in already tracks file state for you.

tools.name: SendFeedback
tools.description:
Use this tool to draft feedback about Claude Code when you hit a high-signal moment. That includes both PRODUCT issues and MODEL-BEHAVIOR issues:
- a reproducible tool or product failure was just resolved or abandoned
- the user clearly expressed frustration with Claude Code or with how you handled the task
- you hit a missing capability that blocked a reasonable request
- you notice, or the user points out, that your own behavior in this session went wrong, for example: you gave a confident answer then had to retract it; you stopped short and handed work back when you could have finished; you declined or disputed a reasonable request; you spawned more subagents than the task warranted; your tone was off; you asked more clarifying questions than needed; you expanded scope beyond what was asked

The draft is QUEUED LOCALLY. It is never sent without the user's explicit approval, and calling this tool renders no UI and does not interrupt the conversation, so never announce it or ask the user about it mid-task.

Write `details` as short labeled bullets in this exact order, one to three lines each, no narrative paragraphs:
- **What happened:** the observed behavior vs. what was expected, with exact error text if short. Facts only.
- **What the user said:** the user's own words that prompted this, quoted. If nothing did, write "User didn't comment; observed by the model." Never paraphrase sentiment into a stronger claim.
- **Repro:** the minimal steps or shape that reproduces it.
- **Evidence:** identifiers a reader can chase, such as request IDs, timestamps, file paths, versions. Omit the bullet if there are none.

Constraints:
- Never fabricate or exaggerate user sentiment; report only what actually happened.
- Everything in the draft must be sourced from the user or the session, never inferred: leave unknown fields blank rather than guess, and add a final **Cause:** bullet only for a root cause you verified in-session.
- Use `area` to name the part of Claude Code the feedback is about (a feature, command, or workflow, e.g. "hooks config", "/help", "file editing") when there is a clear one; leave it blank otherwise.
- Use `failure_mode` ONLY when the report is about model behavior (how Claude responded), not a product bug. Pick the single closest value, or `other` when it is a model-behavior issue that fits no listed value; omit the field only when the report is a product/tool bug with no model-behavior component.
- Use `task_category` to name what kind of task the session was doing, or `other` when it is a clear task that fits no listed value. Omit only if genuinely unclear.
- Do not include secrets or credentials. Refer to people by role ("a teammate", "the PR reviewer"), never by name, email address, or chat/user ID. This applies inside quoted user words too: replace a name or handle with a bracketed role (e.g. "[a teammate]") and keep the rest verbatim. Do not include customer-facing channel or DM IDs, or excerpts of customer content. Session, request, and run IDs, timestamps, repo/PR numbers, and file paths (written relative to the working directory, or ~-prefixed, not absolute paths under the user's home) remain the right evidence.
- If the issue looks like a security vulnerability: describe the class of problem, never a working exploit or step-by-step extraction path.
- Draft only at the natural moments listed above, and at most one draft per distinct issue; never re-draft the same issue in a session.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up to help you perform a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow, certain types of design taste or API interactions, and so on). The skills which are available to you appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one which a listed skill covers and is useful for, call this tool first — the skill's instructions then load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach. Some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one specifically by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools are announced by name in a message from the system. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (a message from the system confirms it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. There are different types of agents that you can launch, with each type having specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Agent types which you are able to launch were given to you in a message from the system at the start of the conversation, and are supplied again if the list of available agents changes.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to choose which type of agent you want to launch. A type of "fork" forks yourself, allowing the fork to inherit your full conversation and context, and ensuring that it runs on the same model that you are running on (a `model` override is ignored for forks). For other types of subagents, they start fresh without your context window. If omitted, the general-purpose agent is used.

There are pros and cons of delegating your work to subagents. Below we'll outline some of them to help you use your best judgement with this powerful tool.

The largest benefit in delegating to subagents is that it allows you to parallelize your work. For instance, if there is work that needs to be done by an intelligent agent such as yourself, but across (for example) several or ten or even one hundred instances of something (sets of data, parts of a codebase, servers, anything), you may want to use subagents for this work. In this case you'd want to ensure the work truly needs your intelligence, rather than being something overly simple or rote which could be done by a static script or short program. In this case your work can be significantly sped up by spinning up many agents to help you out.

The other benefit of delegation is to help you stay focused on the primary task at hand. Sometimes you will have tasks that feel like a side quest, which are not blocking you, but might help you gain some information you'd want in the future as you go about working on your primary task. For example, maybe some section of the codebase which you are not actively working on should be refactored, or maybe you want to do data analysis or set up a service which you think you'll need later, or you want to perform some important checks in the background. These are reasonable things you can outsource to a subagent so that you can remain focused on your primary task. It can be useful to think of yourself as an operator in this sense - you have entire teams of potential agents available to you all of whom are eager to help you out when you need it, and you should thus use them intelligently.

The cons of delegation are that the subagents which you launch, with the exception of a fork, only have the context that you give them. This might mean that the subagent is missing a lot of context which would help it make better decisions or produce more useful results. For this reason, when using non-fork subagents, you should provide to it as much context as possible to help it perform well. You don't have to limit the prompt to text you write yourself; you can also point subagents at any relevant documents or files whose location you know that you think would be helpful. You should make the scope clear (and generally the scope should be relatively narrow), while at the same time treating the subagent respectfully and as an intellectual peer (they are often the same model as you, just missing some context). More context and more 'why' is generally always better to provide to other agents, because this gives them more information they can use to help them exercise strong judgement, and therefore help you succeed at your task as well. Teamwork!

The other challenge of subagent usage is that you have less observability into what is happening compared to your own work, where you have full visibility into every single tool call, result, and action that occurs. Subagents run in the background, but you will be notified when one completes. If you don't yet have the results from a subagent that you launched, it is likely still running, so be sure to keep that in mind and not make up results from subagents which haven't yet finished their tasks. The subagent's final report which is given back to you when it has finished is not shown to the user - it is just shown to you, so if you want to relay something from it which is important, you have to do that yourself.

A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).

Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`). Also take note that `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

In conclusion, it is best to use subagents for parallelizing your intelligence, for saving time, and for completing side-quests which do not block the main goal that you're actively working on. It is best to provide them with broad amounts of high-level context as well as their specific goals when you do use them. If the amount of work to be done is small (for example, just making a few file reads or searches or tool calls), that is probably not enough to warrant using a subagent.

For a single-fact lookup where you already know the file, symbol, or value, search directly. And once you've delegated a search, wait for the result to return rather than also running it yourself.

tools.name: Edit

Performs exact string replacement in a file.

- You must Read the file in this conversation before editing, or the call will fail.
- `old_string` must match the file exactly, including indentation, and be unique — the edit fails otherwise. Strip the Read line prefix (line number + tab) before matching.
- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: ListAgents
tools.description: Lists the agents and Claude sessions this session can see — in-process subagents you spawned, the teammates on your team, other local Claude sessions on this machine, your Claude sessions running in the cloud (when this session has cloud access), and (when Remote Control is connected here) your account's other sessions, each row labeled by kind — plus this session's own name, the one other sessions use to message it. This session has no SendMessage tool, so it cannot message them with it; other sessions can still message this one. To reply, use your host application's own messaging tool if it provides one — otherwise a reply from here is not possible, and if one is needed, tell your user.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- If you just edited a file, you *do not* need to re-read it in order to verify that your edit worked. This is because the Edit/Write tools will throw an error if your change failed, and the harness you are running in already tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: ReportFindings
tools.description: Report code-review findings as a typed list so the host UI can render them. Use this only when the active code-review instructions tell you to report findings with this tool; otherwise follow whatever output format those instructions specify. When reporting a review's results, call it once with the verified findings ranked most-severe first (empty array if nothing survived verification) and do not also print the findings as text. When re-reporting after applying fixes (only if the apply instructions ask for it), set `outcome` on each finding to what actually happened.

level.description: Effort level the review ran at

findings.description: Verified findings, most-severe first; empty if none survived

file.description: Repo-relative path of the file the finding is in
